Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

7B0015C0DFE601310D1B68A86D17958E.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = l w h and V = b h to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

7AFFCD90DFE601310D1A68A86D17958E.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

7AFF7910DFE601310D1968A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
7AFEEBA0DFE601310D1768A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

7AFE97B0DFE601310D1668A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
7AFD3030DFE601310D1268A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

7AFC5460DFE601310D1068A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

7EC25B60DFE6013113F168A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

7EC20B90DFE6013113F068A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7EC16940DFE6013113EE68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

7EC11530DFE6013113ED68A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

7EC0BFC0DFE6013113EC68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

7EC06930DFE6013113EB68A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

7EC01750DFE6013113EA68A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

7EBFC480DFE6013113E968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

7EBF6900DFE6013113E868A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

7EBF0600DFE6013113E768A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7EBEAA50DFE6013113E668A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

7EBE5DE0DFE6013113E568A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

7EBE0D20DFE6013113E468A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

7EBDB980DFE6013113E368A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7EBD55F0DFE6013113E268A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

7EBCF420DFE6013113E168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

7EBCA570DFE6013113E068A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7EBC5160DFE6013113DF68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

7EBBFFB0DFE6013113DE68A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

7EBBA810DFE6013113DD68A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

7EBB43D0DFE6013113DC68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

7EBA4170DFE6013113D968A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7EB95E10DFE6013113D768A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7EB90E10DFE6013113D668A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

7EB8BF80DFE6013113D568A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7EB87030DFE6013113D468A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7EB81960DFE6013113D368A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

7EB7ACF0DFE6013113D268A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

7EB74A50DFE6013113D168A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7EB6B1B0DFE6013113CF68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

7EB65C30DFE6013113CE68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7EB60670DFE6013113CD68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7EB55EC0DFE6013113CB68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

7EB50280DFE6013113CA68A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7EB49760DFE6013113C968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7EB44380DFE6013113C868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

7EB3F2F0DFE6013113C768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

7EB3A0A0DFE6013113C668A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

7EB2FC40DFE6013113C468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

7EB29DF0DFE6013113C368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

7EB247D0DFE6013113C268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

7EB19160DFE6013113C068A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

7EB14350DFE6013113BF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

7EB0DFA0DFE6013113BE68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

7EB045A0DFE6013113BC68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

7EAFF6B0DFE6013113BB68A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7EAFA410DFE6013113BA68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7EAF4EC0DFE6013113B968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

7EAEF840DFE6013113B868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

7EAEA830DFE6013113B768A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

7EADFF20DFE6013113B568A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

7EADA0E0DFE6013113B468A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

7EAD3970DFE6013113B368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

7EAC8B30DFE6013113B168A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

7EAC1B30DFE6013113B068A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

7EABB0C0DFE6013113AF68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

7EAB05C0DFE6013113AD68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

7EAAB200DFE6013113AC68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

7EAA5E00DFE6013113AB68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7EAA0AE0DFE6013113AA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

7EA9AE20DFE6013113A968A86D17958E.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

7EA960E0DFE6013113A868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

7EA8B5E0DFE6013113A668A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

7EA83C40DFE6013113A568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

7EA7DA90DFE6013113A468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

7EA74140DFE6013113A268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

7EA6EEF0DFE6013113A168A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

7EA67E00DFE6013113A068A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7EA56A50DFE60131139D68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

7EA51E80DFE60131139C68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7EA477E0DFE60131139A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

7EA41D90DFE60131139968A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

7EA36B30DFE60131139768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

7EA30FA0DFE60131139668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

7EA2A0B0DFE60131139568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

7EA1FAA0DFE60131139368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

7EA1AAD0DFE60131139268A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

7EA15700DFE60131139168A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7EA03A90DFE60131138E68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

7E9FF000DFE60131138D68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7E9FA370DFE60131138C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

7E9F5590DFE60131138B68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

7E9F0400DFE60131138A68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

7E9E0BB0DFE60131138768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

7E9DB770DFE60131138668A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

7E9CFF60DFE60131138468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

7E9CB060DFE60131138368A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

7E9C5C20DFE60131138268A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

7E9B9AE0DFE60131138068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Montana Common Core Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

7E237470DFE6013112AE68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

7E22FDA0DFE6013112AD68A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

7E22A800DFE6013112AC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

7E225F90DFE6013112AB68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

7E221620DFE6013112AA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7E21CC00DFE6013112A968A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

7E218060DFE6013112A868A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

7E213100DFE6013112A768A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

7E20DFD0DFE6013112A668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

7E205200DFE6013112A468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

7E200A30DFE6013112A368A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

7E1FC1D0DFE6013112A268A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

7E1F24F0DFE6013112A068A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

7E1ED140DFE60131129F68A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

7E1E80A0DFE60131129E68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

7E1E2DA0DFE60131129D68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.

7E1DD970DFE60131129C68A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.

7E1D74F0DFE60131129B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7E1CE400DFE60131129968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

7E1C9CB0DFE60131129868A86D17958E.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

7E1C53A0DFE60131129768A86D17958E.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

7E1C0950DFE60131129668A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

7E1BB480DFE60131129568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7E1AD670DFE60131129268A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

7E1A8BA0DFE60131129168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7E1A3920DFE60131129068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7E199360DFE60131128E68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

7E18E6B0DFE60131128C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7E189850DFE60131128B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7E17F5F0DFE60131128968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

7E17A780DFE60131128868A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

7E175F90DFE60131128768A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

7E171790DFE60131128668A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

7E167550DFE60131128468A86D17958E.description: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.

7E162800DFE60131128368A86D17958E.description: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

7E15DB00DFE60131128268A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.

7E158A10DFE60131128168A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.

7E153F40DFE60131128068A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

7E14EF90DFE60131127F68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

7E148D10DFE60131127E68A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

7E138880DFE60131127B68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7E131AA0DFE60131127A68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

7E12C680DFE60131127968A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7E122550DFE60131127768A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

7E11DB60DFE60131127668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

7E118F20DFE60131127568A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7E10ECC0DFE60131127368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

7E10A4D0DFE60131127268A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7E100690DFE60131127068A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point[s]").

7E0F9890DFE60131126F68A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or a drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., how characters interact]").

7E0F41F0DFE60131126E68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7E0EEB80DFE60131126D68A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.

7E0EA420DFE60131126C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

7E0E5960DFE60131126B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7E0E0A40DFE60131126A68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two pages in a single sitting.

7E0DB660DFE60131126968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

7E0D6AC0DFE60131126868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

7E0CC5C0DFE60131126668A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

7E0C6470DFE60131126568A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

7E0C0900DFE60131126468A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

7E0BC160DFE60131126368A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

7E0B7880DFE60131126268A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

7E0B2EC0DFE60131126168A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

7E0AE1F0DFE60131126068A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

7E0A8AE0DFE60131125F68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

7E0A24C0DFE60131125E68A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).

7E09D000DFE60131125D68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

7E098450DFE60131125C68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7E093C60DFE60131125B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

7E08F450DFE60131125A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

7E08AAA0DFE60131125968A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

7E085430DFE60131125868A86D17958E.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

7E080810DFE60131125768A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

7E07BB10DFE60131125668A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

7E06B160DFE60131125368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7E061600DFE60131125168A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7E05CC40DFE60131125068A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

7E0582F0DFE60131124F68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7E0539B0DFE60131124E68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7E04EBD0DFE60131124D68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

7E048740DFE60131124C68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

7E043A60DFE60131124B68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7E03A930DFE60131124968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

7E035D90DFE60131124868A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7E030110DFE60131124768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7E024A50DFE60131124568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

7E01FAB0DFE60131124468A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

7E01A550DFE60131124368A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

7E013CF0DFE60131124268A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

7E00E480DFE60131124168A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

7E004BD0DFE60131123F68A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

7DFFFF70DFE60131123E68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

7DFF0940DFE60131123B68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7DFEC0A0DFE60131123A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7DFE7680DFE60131123968A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

7DFE29E0DFE60131123868A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

7DFDD4A0DFE60131123768A86D17958E.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

7DFD09E0DFE60131123568A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.

7DFCBA70DFE60131123468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.

7DFC6FA0DFE60131123368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

7DFBB3D0DFE60131123168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.

7DFB56A0DFE60131123068A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.

7DFB0F10DFE60131122F68A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

7DFA3460DFE60131122C68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7DF9EAD0DFE60131122B68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7DF94380DFE60131122968A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.

7DF8F2B0DFE60131122868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

7DF83EA0DFE60131122668A86D17958E.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.

7DF7E7E0DFE60131122568A86D17958E.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

7DF793B0DFE60131122468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

7DF70380DFE60131122268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

7DF6B8E0DFE60131122168A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.

7DF669D0DFE60131122068A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

7DF54CF0DFE60131121D68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

7DF4FFA0DFE60131121C68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7DF4B6B0DFE60131121B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

7DF46670DFE60131121A68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

7DF3F860DFE60131121968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

7DF309E0DFE60131121668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

7DF2BCB0DFE60131121568A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

7DF20E70DFE60131121368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

7DF1C1E0DFE60131121268A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

7DF17180DFE60131121168A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Montana Common Core Standards for Mathematical Practices and Mathematics Content

7ABFA500DFE601310CCB68A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.
7ABF6390DFE601310CCA68A86D17958E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

7ABF1E70DFE601310CC968A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
comments: Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

7ABED490DFE601310CC868A86D17958E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?
7ABE8720DFE601310CC768A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

7ABE29E0DFE601310CC668A86D17958E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

7ABDC100DFE601310CC568A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

7ABD7A80DFE601310CC468A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

7ABD2410DFE601310CC368A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

7ABCCFB0DFE601310CC268A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

7ABC86D0DFE601310CC168A86D17958E.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

7ABC3BE0DFE601310CC068A86D17958E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

7ABBF2A0DFE601310CBF68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

7ABBA320DFE601310CBE68A86D17958E.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

7ABB54B0DFE601310CBD68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

7ABAEB40DFE601310CBC68A86D17958E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

7ABAAA60DFE601310CBB68A86D17958E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

7ABA2500DFE601310CB968A86D17958E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

7AB9E120DFE601310CB868A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

7AB99DE0DFE601310CB768A86D17958E.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

7AB95590DFE601310CB668A86D17958E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

7AB8BB60DFE601310CB468A86D17958E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

7AB87460DFE601310CB368A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

7AB82FC0DFE601310CB268A86D17958E.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

7AB7ED90DFE601310CB168A86D17958E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

7AB7A540DFE601310CB068A86D17958E.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

7AB75750DFE601310CAF68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

7AB5FC10DFE601310CAA68A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

7AB71540DFE601310CAE68A86D17958E.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

7AB6D330DFE601310CAD68A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

7AB68EF0DFE601310CAC68A86D17958E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …

7AB646A0DFE601310CAB68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

7AB3E9F0DFE601310CA368A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

7AB39830DFE601310CA268A86D17958E.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

7AB34450DFE601310CA168A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

7AB2EC50DFE601310CA068A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

7AB517A0DFE601310CA768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

7AB4D4E0DFE601310CA668A86D17958E.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

7AB48EE0DFE601310CA568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

7AB44460DFE601310CA468A86D17958E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

7AB28420DFE601310C9F68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

7AB21AB0DFE601310C9E68A86D17958E.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

7AB19400DFE601310C9C68A86D17958E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1—100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is prime or composite.

7AB15140DFE601310C9B68A86D17958E.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

7AB10D60DFE601310C9A68A86D17958E.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

7AB0CA30DFE601310C9968A86D17958E.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

7AB08200DFE601310C9868A86D17958E.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

7AB03840DFE601310C9768A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

7AAFAED0DFE601310C9568A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
7AAF5DE0DFE601310C9468A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

7AADD660DFE601310C9068A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
