7FFF57E0DFE6013116B068A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7FFEFE40DFE6013116AF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

7FFEAFF0DFE6013116AE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole, paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

7FFE6030DFE6013116AD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7FFE0480DFE6013116AC68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

7FFDB340DFE6013116AB68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

7FFD6490DFE6013116AA68A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

7FFD1470DFE6013116A968A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

7FFCC4B0DFE6013116A868A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 11—12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

7FFBFB50DFE6013116A668A86D17958E.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

7FFB99A0DFE6013116A568A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

7FFA4B20DFE6013116A168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7FF9F1E0DFE6013116A068A86D17958E.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage, Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

7FF99170DFE60131169F68A86D17958E.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested.

7FF93B80DFE60131169E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7FF83D80DFE60131169B68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7FF79D70DFE60131169968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7FF74B10DFE60131169868A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7FF68690DFE60131169668A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

7FF5DB80DFE60131169468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7FF59000DFE60131169368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7FF4EEA0DFE60131169168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

7FF49900DFE60131169068A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7FF43AA0DFE60131168F68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

7FF3CE10DFE60131168E68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed, and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

7FF30700DFE60131168C68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

7FF2BB40DFE60131168B68A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

7FF26EE0DFE60131168A68A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

7FF21F00DFE60131168968A86D17958E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

7FF1BF40DFE60131168868A86D17958E.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

7FF16CA0DFE60131168768A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

7FF12020DFE60131168668A86D17958E.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 11—12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7FF033F0DFE60131168368A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7FEFD410DFE60131168268A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

7FEF7880DFE60131168168A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7FEEBEE0DFE60131167F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

7FEE5C00DFE60131167E68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

7FEDFE00DFE60131167D68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7FED6130DFE60131167B68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

7FED1140DFE60131167A68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7FEC1880DFE60131167868A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7FEBC840DFE60131167768A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the specific task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and over-reliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

7FEB7840DFE60131167668A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7FEB2720DFE60131167568A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7FEAC1C0DFE60131167468A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

7FEA6590DFE60131167368A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

7FEA08D0DFE60131167268A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7FE96300DFE60131167068A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation provided (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

7FE91120DFE60131166F68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic; convey a knowledgeable stance in a style that responds to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.

7FE8B420DFE60131166E68A86D17958E.description: Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

7FE85C10DFE60131166D68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

7FE80B80DFE60131166C68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic and organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7FE7BF90DFE60131166B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

7FE77380DFE60131166A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

7FE72550DFE60131166968A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

7FE6CB40DFE60131166868A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

7FE67F30DFE60131166768A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

7FE63300DFE60131166668A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

7FE5E3F0DFE60131166568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

7FE52DF0DFE60131166368A86D17958E.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

7FE4C5C0DFE60131166268A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7FE41210DFE60131166068A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses]").

7FE3C160DFE60131165F68A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

7FE36FC0DFE60131165E68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7FE308B0DFE60131165D68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and over-reliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

7FE2B2C0DFE60131165C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7FE264B0DFE60131165B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7FE21730DFE60131165A68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

7FE1C920DFE60131165968A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

7FE17900DFE60131165868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7FE0D310DFE60131165668A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

7FE082D0DFE60131165568A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

7FE02BC0DFE60131165468A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

7FDFD2A0DFE60131165368A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

7FDF73B0DFE60131165268A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

7FDF1E90DFE60131165168A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

7FDED3B0DFE60131165068A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

7FDE88B0DFE60131164F68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

7FDE3BF0DFE60131164E68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

7FDDED10DFE60131164D68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

7FDD9160DFE60131164C68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

7FDD16F0DFE60131164B68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7FDCAEE0DFE60131164A68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7FDC5CE0DFE60131164968A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

7FDC04A0DFE60131164868A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

7FDBAA40DFE60131164768A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

7FDB56A0DFE60131164668A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

7FDAFAE0DFE60131164568A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

7FDA95C0DFE60131164468A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7FD98A20DFE60131164168A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7FD8F640DFE60131163F68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7FD8AAE0DFE60131163E68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

7FD85BE0DFE60131163D68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7FD80740DFE60131163C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7FD7B650DFE60131163B68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

7FD76310DFE60131163A68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

7FD71700DFE60131163968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7FD66EE0DFE60131163768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

7FD61FB0DFE60131163668A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7FD5C9F0DFE60131163568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7FD521D0DFE60131163368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

7FD4C5C0DFE60131163268A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7FD47B80DFE60131163168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7FD42F90DFE60131163068A86D17958E.description: Synthesize information from a range of sources (e.g., texts, experiments, simulations) into a coherent understanding of a process, phenomenon, or concept, resolving conflicting information when possible.

7FD3E270DFE60131162F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in a science or technical text, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

7FD390E0DFE60131162E68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., quantitative data, video, multimedia) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

7FD2C980DFE60131162C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, identifying important issues that remain unresolved.

7FD26B30DFE60131162B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the text structures information or ideas into categories or hierarchies, demonstrating understanding of the information or ideas.

7FD20FD0DFE60131162A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 11—12 texts and topics.

7FD14820DFE60131162868A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks; analyze the specific results based on explanations in the text.

7FD0ED60DFE60131162768A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; summarize complex concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms.

7FD0A2C0DFE60131162668A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to important distinctions the author makes and to any gaps or inconsistencies in the account.

7FD00B80DFE60131162468A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

7FCFBD70DFE60131162368A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7FCF6AA0DFE60131162268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7FCF0CF0DFE60131162168A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

7FCEBFF0DFE60131162068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

7FCE6820DFE60131161F68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

7FCDA0C0DFE60131161D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

7FCD48A0DFE60131161C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

7FCCF960DFE60131161B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

7FCC5010DFE60131161968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

7FCBEAF0DFE60131161868A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

7FCB9110DFE60131161768A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

7FCAF660DFE60131161568A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

7FCAA5C0DFE60131161468A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7FCA5090DFE60131161368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7FC9F480DFE60131161268A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

7FC99D10DFE60131161168A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

7FC94330DFE60131161068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

7FC87740DFE60131160E68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

7FC81D60DFE60131160D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

7FC7D050DFE60131160C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

7FC73500DFE60131160A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

7FC6E310DFE60131160968A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

7FC68050DFE60131160868A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

7FC572A0DFE60131160568A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7FC527A0DFE60131160468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7FC48DF0DFE60131160268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

7FC43260DFE60131160168A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

7FC37E10DFE6013115FF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

document.title: Essential Understandings Regarding Montana Indians Key Concepts

39C164A24FD44E6CAA1759835D253B34.description:
Despite the complex evolution of tribal sovereignty in America, it remains one of the most
important attributes of tribal independence.

299E377688504598AE4C33D6443C1970.description: The extent and breadth of self-governing powers is not the same for every tribe.

61FF4748405C46D9B4AEDADDCCDB78CF.description:
In general, tribes are free to exercise any of their sovereign powers unless Congress has
specifically limited or modified them in some way.

5BC9B938908E4C9F81ECC23AA0497EB0.description:
Some limitations have been placed on tribal sovereignty throughout the past two centuries by
Supreme Court rulings and Congressional statues, which is why tribes are sometimes referred
to as “limited” sovereigns today.

8B9BACD994F64084836D54DFA475F676.description:
Tribal self-governing powers predate the existence of the United States and are not delegated
powers granted by Congress or any other entity; they are inherent powers of sovereign nations
that have never been extinguished.

878224DCDC2E4CC4A87659D076DBB639.description:
Tribal sovereignty stems directly from the fact that tribal nations constitute distinct political
communities that have the right to determine their own laws and form of government.

EC42B785FEEC4C38B1AE8CD1D6F284FA.description:
American Indian tribal nations are inherent sovereign nations and they possess sovereign powers,
separate and independent from the federal and state governments. However, under the American
legal system, the extent and breadth of self-governing powers are not the same for each tribe.

39AF262CCDD240D89503753B0F25C4B9.description:
By giving students the opportunity to view our past through the eyes of many, they can begin to
create their own view of our collective history, understand the present, and become better
prepared to engage the problems of the future.

9645EC44DF6E4B0F8EFB64199FE2A60D.description:
Providing students with textbooks, primary source documents, and surviving oral traditions
allows them to gain a more objective view of history and provides them with a historical
context in which to situate and understand the experiences and perspectives of these groups in
American society today.

8C5EE64E964E414CB20DF20CB06BE5E8.description:
It is critical that history curricula include the stories and experiences of individual men and
women of diverse racial, ethnic, and religious groups.

42BBC92A2FB444C5B13AC6E7939189D6.description:
History is a primary vehicle through which power is distributed and used; thus, the whole
notion of political identity and ideology and who the United States is as a nation plays into how
the story is told, and who has been privileged to tell the story.

2CDC41F9B414484C89EF7169E9836459.description: A huge amount of political capital is involved in the telling of history.

E8FDA7F9927141369C6B810155BBBB1F.description:
Much of America’s history has been told from the Euro-American perspective. Only recently
have American Indians begun to write about and retell history from an indigenous perspective.

96CA6FF8B17040B3B7BD9A597516AB8A.description: History is a story most often related through the subjective experience of the teller.

D9C269882583437791BEAA039D12A78E.description:
History is a story most often related through the subjective experience of the teller. With the
inclusion of more and varied voices, histories are being rediscovered and revised. History told from
American Indian perspectives frequently conflicts with the stories mainstream historians tell.

62187B29BF434A7BB1EF241A64432B50.description:
Although the history of federal Indian policy is long and complex, understanding its main
legislative pieces and outcomes helps provide context for the contemporary experiences of
Indian students and communities.

A28A5F55140942B98B3D94F2A0C706CC.description:
Federal Indian policies have fluctuated between respecting tribal sovereignty and terminating
tribes’ sovereign status altogether.

749BFACF6EF64D9981A093887A7BA119.description:
Early in American history, Congress exerted extensive power over Indians and since has enacted
over four hundred treaties and statutes dealing with Native Americans. Regulations and
guidelines implementing these laws are even more numerous, making American Indians the
most regulated population in the United States.

AED24E972C4F45A9956BEFDE7C1BF3EE.description:
The complexity of contemporary American Indian rights and sovereignty can be difficult to
decipher; however, this history can be easier to understand when it is divided into major
federal policy periods.

D8934EE1A4904365B3B33715DD85CE74.description:
There were many federal policies put into place throughout American history that have affected
Indian people in the past and continue to shape who they are today. Many of these policies
conflicted with one another. Much of Indian history can be related through several major federal
policy periods: Colonization/Colonial Period (1492 - 1800s), Treaty-Making and Removal Period
(1778 – 1871), Reservation Period - Allotment and Assimilation (1887 – 1934), Tribal Reorganization
Period (1934 – 1953), Termination and Relocation Period (1953 – 1968), Self-Determination Period
(1975 - Present)

D7E66A39E02C4E2BBEAA73BCDE66F14E.description:
After Congress officially ended treaty-making with tribes in 1871, the federal government used
other means to further reduce Indian landholdings on reservations.

2AC3BB624ACD44D796A39316F4D1C61F.description: There are two main treaties that affected Montana tribal lands:

03D0A6B889D54CE9AC52431944AB53AA.description: Today, there are 326 reservations in the United States, seven of which are located in Montana.

33CE3F013CE2495380565C0C9BBA60E9.description:
Indian tribes fought to protect their lands and resources including actively utilizing American
courts and the Indian Claims Commission.

46E9031A1AC14AE8A9C41DC2F4FA834B.description:
Original Indian title to land was acknowledged by tribes and European nations, as well as the
United States.

2A440227C0F14EA5A8DE8CFBBFA40E27.description:
Some reservations are the remnants of a tribe’s original land base while others were created by
Congressional statute or executive order for the resettling of Indian people forcibly relocated
from their homelands.

50FF54CECD83456CABCE6AEF3F9FA3DE.description:
Reservations are lands that have been reserved by tribes or for tribes for their exclusive use as
permanent homelands.

7A6860678B604EC389198B8E8A330D51.description:
Though there have been tribal peoples living successfully on the North American lands for millennia,
reservations are lands that have been reserved by or for tribes for their exclusive use as permanent
homelands. Some were created through treaties while others were created by statutes and
executive orders. The principle that land should be acquired from tribes only through their consent
with treaties involved three assumptions: Both parties to treaties were sovereign powers. Indian
tribes had some form of transferable title to the land. Acquisition of Indian lands was solely a
government matter not to be left to individual colonists or states.

5D160AB507934B7FBB3ED55D2D87540A.description:
Educators should be aware that portions of these principles and values are private and are to
be used and understood by certain individuals, groups, or the entire tribe. Tribal culture
bearers, experts, and others can assist educators in navigating these situations.

D3A5097AEC8D4C0680437B21A66D6BE8.description:
Tribal oral traditions, ideologies, worldviews, and the principles and values associated with
them, are as valid as other such traditions from around the world and should be accorded the
same respect and standing.

358D2B08D57A479AB7F222588D82264E.description: Humor plays an important role in American Indian cultures, there was no “stoic” Indian.

FB32CF1D62BE48798B224A881A09AB75.description:
It is not important for educators to understand all the complexities of modern day American
Indian cultures; however, they should be aware of their existence and the fact they can
influence much of the thinking and practice of American Indians today.

5D15CC6C678E48EBACB8F1AEE4891BCD.description:
Despite this history, Native people have retained their spiritual beliefs and traditions – tribal
languages are still spoken, sacred songs are still sung, and rituals and ceremonies are still
performed.

67793D926E97450CA8AC8A289B227B79.description:
A complex history of pre-Columbian tribal migrations and intertribal interactions, European
colonization and Christianization efforts, and federal assimilation policies have contributed to
the broad range of spiritual beliefs held by American Indians today.

367C1D8C112A4D36ADBBBAADAD045EC8.description:
The term spirituality within a cultural context can be limiting and misconstrued. Spirituality to
Indigenous peoples generally refers to one aspect of their worldview in which all things are
connected. Spirituality in this context does not necessarily equate to nor denote religion.

E6A45113C351458A852A275BC2824817.description:
The ideologies of Native traditional beliefs and spirituality persist into modern day life as tribal
cultures, traditions, and languages are still practiced by many American Indian people and are
incorporated into how tribes govern and manage their affairs.
Additionally, each tribe has its own oral histories, which are as valid as written histories. These
histories predate the “discovery” of North America.

D33BF220667E4CDDA69C33982D272D95.description:
Ideally, school curricula will offer equal recognition of the contributions students’ home
cultures bring to the learning situation and will help all students develop the self-esteem and
self-confidence that can enhance their learning.

3B07F0130AC64D0EBB531A52FFEA138E.description:
Students who maintain a strong sense of pride in their language and culture tend not to
experience school failure.

6A52A7961A214FC08E28E91DE206FDC3.description:
Boarding schools and other federal policies of assimilation brought disruptions to the
traditional transference of knowledge in tribal communities and have had wide-ranging and
lasting impacts on American Indian individuals and communities.

B689ABCDD2EE4923A190D75C1DBE56F9.description:
For millennia, individual tribal groups successfully educated their children using highly effective
indigenous pedagogies that imbued Indian children with all the knowledge and skills they
needed to thrive in their world.

5D92F38D757F434B98CA2B1CE4503B23.description:
There exists no universally accepted rule for establishing an individual’s identity as Indian.
However, as a general rule, an Indian is a person who has some biological Indian ancestry and is
recognized as an Indian by a tribe.

0AEDF21A3DA0448EB410E07A8776961B.description:
Just as there is great diversity among tribal nations, there is great diversity among individual
American Indians as identity is developed, defined, and redefined by entities, organizations, and
people. There is no generic American Indian.

163F1575FC6047AE8C729D89763F40C8.description:
American Indian individuals and tribes are still here with distinct and intact governments,
languages, and cultures that contribute to modern Montana.

8E809EE86651448DA1B1024AC47BE6E6.description:
The political, demographic, and cultural landscape of Montana has rapidly changed in the last
two hundred years.

DDF0A83C0F784C23843DD8DA2869E535.description:
Tribal governments are fully functioning governments that provide an array of services similar
to those of federal, state, and local governments.

DA4938971BC1413AB7921FDB99C3311D.description: Tribal sovereignty is the inherent right of tribes to independent self-governance.

AED43A2E58204C0CACAA1BBEE9F21812.description:
The twelve sovereign tribes, located in what is now the state of Montana, are distinct from one
another in their history, culture, and language.

AC9A7A4899FC43228899783C998534CE.description:
There is great diversity among the twelve sovereign tribes of Montana in their languages, cultures,
histories, and governments. Each tribe has a distinct and unique cultural heritage that contributes to
modern Montana.

document.title: Montana World Languages Content Standards & Performance Descriptors 2026

CE67B046D9814C17AD50F8C7303A1CCD.description: School, local, and global communities: Learners use the language, both within and beyond the classroom, to interact and collaborate with their local, state, and global communities, including Montana Indigenous Nations.

8ADB9582A8424DD69963541B45A0BF20.description: Communicate and interact with cultural competence in order to participate in multilingual communities at home and around the world.

D1D1564989034B8DB95E2CAD2F3CE971.description: Cultural comparisons: Learners use the language to investigate, explain, and reflect on the concept of culture through comparisons between the cultures, their own way of life, and Montana Indigenous culture's history, diversity, and sovereignty

C7C6ACE07BB7439C9CA3D7C076DBE3B2.description: Language comparisons: Learners use the language to investigate, explain, and reflect on the nature of language through comparisons of the language studied, their own language, and, when appropriate, Montana Indigenous Languages.

2F8A48B5C78040B5A3DD09D9B10964D5.description: Develop insight into the nature of language and culture to interact with cultural competence, with a particular emphasis on Montana Indigenous cultures.

A3F694EB02B14B7A85BE4107A760CD49.description: Acquiring information and diverse perspectives: Learners access and evaluate information and diverse perspectives that are available through studying the language and its cultures.

B01110AAFBFE4208BCFB580D4538A9BE.description: Making connections: Learners build, reinforce, and expand their knowledge of other disciplines while using the language to develop critical thinking and solve problems creatively.

FC2DC7338A3B46AB8075B1B511EEEA9E.description: Connect with other disciplines and acquire information and diverse perspectives, including Montana Tribes, in order to use the language to function in academic and career-related situations.

0CA9042B067C4D378C1C3DDC484F9A14.description: Relating cultural products to perspectives: Learners use the language to investigate, explain, and reflect on the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied, and, where appropriate, the cultures of Montana Indigenous Tribes.

EE5B8319B95743A2A4DDD8D61ABF37C5.description: Relating cultural practices to perspectives: Learners use the language to investigate, explain, and reflect on the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures studied, and, where appropriate, the cultures of Montana Indigenous Tribes.

E1FC7C9513E94FA793C1D2105314366E.description: Interact with cultural competence and understanding.

631A363DD95842DC98C6087E6081B3E1.description: Presentational communication: Learners present information, concepts, and ideas pertaining to a variety of topics using appropriate media and adapting to various audiences of listeners, readers, or viewers in order to inform, explain, persuade, and narrate.

BDDF0D6580424172B4A8CE1C63DB0E94.description: When learners hear, read, or view a variety of topics in the target language, they can understand a variety of topics; interpret a variety of topics; and analyze a variety of topics.

9955326F1E2249599C866BEFF4C9534F.description: Interpersonal communication: Learners interact and negotiate meaning in spoken, signed, or written conversations to share information, reactions, feelings, and opinions

A48A446CC8FF46EDB463D2C11872F1BC.description: Communicate effectively in more than one language in order to function in a variety of situations and for multiple purposes.
